perItem.what: In `callOrsOptimization` (route-optimization.service.ts, ORS parser block): the response type now also declares `unassigned?: Array<{ id?: number }>` (vroom shape). The step-derived ids became `assignedIds`; `unassignedIds` maps `data.unassigned` job ids (sorted ascending = the original relative stop order, since jobs are emitted as `i + 1`) back to stop ids, dropping nulls, out-of-range ids and any id already scheduled (an `assigned` Set that grows as ids are accepted, so a stop reported twice — or both scheduled and reported — is persisted exactly once). `optimizedIds = [...assignedIds, ...unassignedIds]`, so the unassigned stops are APPENDED as late stops and the primary solver is kept; the existing `optimizedIds.length !== stops.length` throw now fires only on a TRUE mismatch (a stop ORS neither scheduled nor reported), with its message and counts unchanged. Nothing else in the ORS path changed: the vehicle `time_window` is kept, job windows untouched, `fallbackReason` stays unset because no exception is raised, and the post-solve `applyWindowPass` reports the appended stops in `windowViolations` (late by construction — the repair loop finds no feasible position, so it re-inserts each at its original relative index, which is last).
perItem.pin: REG-B177: an ORS response with unassigned jobs keeps the primary solver — 3 stops on the ORS branch (no Google key, `ors.apiKey` = 'ors-key'), fetch resolves `routes[0].steps` for jobs 1 and 2 plus `unassigned: [{ id: 3 }]` where stop 3 (`stop-late`, 0.3 deg north of a (0,0) depot, window 08:00-08:30) is unreachable before its close from an 08:00 departure in any order. Asserts `result.stopOrder` = [stop-ors-a, stop-ors-b, stop-late] (3 stops, unassigned last), `windowViolations` has length 1 with `stopId === 'stop-late'` and `windowEnd === '08:30'`, `usedFallback === false`, `fallbackReason === undefined`, and `fetch` called exactly once. Pre-fix this test fails on values, not existence: steps(2) !== stops(3) threw, so usedFallback would be true and fallbackReason 'ORS_NETWORK_ERROR' with a nearest-neighbour order. Companion pin: REG-B177: an ORS response that neither schedules nor reports a stop still throws — calls the parser directly with 3 stops, `steps: [job 1]`, `unassigned: []`, and asserts `rejects.toThrow("ORS stop count mismatch: expected 3, got 1")` so appending the unassigned cannot soften a real mismatch.

perItem.evidence:
Traced end to end in route-optimization.service.ts (read-only, git diff + sed).

PARSER (callOrsOptimization, ~:1364-1405): the response type gains `unassigned?: Array<{ id?: number }>`. `assignedIds` = the old step-derived ids (unchanged). `unassignedIds` = `data.unassigned` → `.map(u => u.id)` → drop null → `.sort((a,b) => a-b)` → `stops[id-1]?.id` → filter through a growing `assigned` Set. The ascending sort IS original relative stop order because the request builds `jobs: stops.map((s,i) => ({ id: i+1, ... }))` (verified at :1346-1354), so job id n ⇔ stops[n-1]. `optimizedIds = [...assignedIds, ...unassignedIds]`.

TRUE-MISMATCH THROW still fires (:1408-1412), byte-identical message/counts. I refuted three ways of softening it: (i) an out-of-range unassigned id (e.g. `{id: 99}` with 3 stops) → `stops[98]?.id` is undefined → filtered → length short → throws; (ii) an id already in `steps` → `assigned.has(id)` → filtered → length short → throws; (iii) `unassigned: []` with 1 of 3 steps → throws "ORS stop count mismatch: expected 3, got 1", which is exactly the companion pin at spec:1172. So the throw cannot be bought off by padding.

APPENDED ORDER → WINDOW PASS → RESULT: optimizeTemplate :549-558 maps optimizedIds back to StopWithCoords and runs applyWindowPass. For the pinned fixture (depot 0,0; stop-late at lat 0.3 = 33.36 km = 40.0 min at 50 km/h; window 08:00-08:30; departure 08:00) `calculateETAs` gives arrival > 08:30 in EVERY position, so the re-insertion loop finds no feasible slot; the not-inserted branch re-inserts at `Math.min(orderedStops.indexOf(stop)=2, remaining.length=2)` = index 2 → LAST. `repaired.length (1) <= violations.length (1)` and no new stopId, so the repaired order is kept. Persisted: the two-phase `$transaction` at :569-587 writes stopNumbers 1..3 over ALL three stops — the unassigned stop really is persisted, not dropped.

fallbackReason: no exception is raised on this path, so `usedFallback` stays false and `fallbackReason` stays undefined (the only writers are the two catch blocks at :536 / :747). Confirmed the ORS branch is entered once — `fetch` is called exactly once, asserted at spec:1170.

Pin REG-B177 "an ORS response with unassigned jobs keeps the primary solver" (spec:1074-1171) asserts values, not existence: stopOrder === [stop-ors-a, stop-ors-b, stop-late], windowViolations length 1 with stopId/windowEnd values, usedFallback false, fallbackReason undefined, fetch called once. perItem.item: finding 0 (minor) — seed effect keeps `startTime` in its deps, so clearing Departure Time snaps back to the tenant default; the two dispatch modals diverge
perItem.evidence:
Both modals now carry `const seededRef = React.useRef(false)` and the identical one-shot effect (routes/page.tsx:134-142, templates/[id]/page.tsx:320-328), deps `[open, routeSettings?.defaultStartTime]` — `startTime` is gone from the deps.

CLEAR PATH (both files): operator empties the <input type="time"> → onChange → setStartTime("") → neither dep changed → the seed effect does NOT re-run → the field stays empty. `handleDispatch` sends `startTime: startTime || undefined` (routes/page.tsx:200-206, templates:372-379), so an emptied field means "use the server default", and the debounced analyze effect re-runs once with `startTime: undefined`, so the warning and the dispatch describe the same clock. Pre-fix, templates' effect read `startTime` without declaring it and routes/page.tsx declared it — either way the `!startTime` guard re-seeded the emptied field. Refuted.

REOPEN PATH: both DispatchModals are rendered unconditionally with an `open` prop (routes/page.tsx:744, templates:1250), so they stay MOUNTED and the ref genuinely needs the close-reset it has. On close the effect's `!open` branch sets seededRef.current = false; on the next open it re-seeds. Effect ordering on open in routes/page.tsx is safe: the reset effect (:119-127, deps [open, today]) sets startTime("") and runs BEFORE the seed effect in declaration order, so the batched result is the tenant default, not "".

DIVERGENCE closed: the two effects are now byte-identical apart from the cross-reference comment.

Gate caveat, not a fix defect: the ruled web eslint gate cannot report on this change in this worktree — apps/web/node_modules/eslint is 8.57.1 while the root is 9.39.4 (I confirmed both versions read-only), so @typescript-eslint loads the v9 base rule into the v8 linter and throws before linting anything. I independently checked that the change introduces no new lint surface: every problem the executor's root-eslint-9 diagnostic reported is pre-existing — `cn` is imported-and-unused on master too (`git show master:...` line 15), and `drivers.map((d: any)` is on master at line 148. react-hooks/exhaustive-deps fired twice elsewhere in the templates file and NOT on either new seed effect, which is the load-bearing signal: the new deps are exhaustive, and the brief's "remove the eslint-disable" was a no-op because that effect never carried one (the file's only disable sits on the analyze effect and is untouched).

newHazards.summary: `unassigned` entries are not filtered by `type` the way `steps` are
newHazards.detail: The steps parser filters `s.type === "job"` before trusting `s.job`, but the new unassigned parser takes `u.id` from every entry regardless of type (the declared shape is `{ id?: number }`, with no `type`). Vroom's `unassigned` array can also carry `shipment` and `break` entries whose ids live in their own id spaces, so such an entry's id would be silently mapped onto `stops[id-1]` — a wrong stop appended, or (if out of range) a spurious count mismatch. RouteFlow sends only jobs today, so this is unreachable in practice; it is an asymmetry in defensiveness worth one `.filter(u => u.type === undefined || u.type === "job")` rather than a live defect. Not a land blocker.

newHazards.summary: Underway run with no caller clock: unassigned stops are appended with no window pass and no violation reported
newHazards.detail: In optimizeRoute, `windowClock` is null for an IN_PROGRESS run with no `startTimeOverride`, so the whole window pass is skipped (`if (windowClock)` at :762) and no vehicle `time_window` is sent. If vroom nevertheless returns `unassigned` entries (a job whose own absolute `time_windows` are infeasible), the new parser now APPENDS those stops in original relative order and the service persists that order untouched — no repair, `windowViolations: []`, and the only signal is `windowsChecked: false`. Before this round the same response threw and the run fell back to nearest-neighbour, which at least produced a geometrically sensible order. Failure scenario: a driver re-optimizes mid-run from the mobile app (no clock sent), one stop has an already-closed window, and that stop is driven last purely because vroom dropped it — with nothing in the result naming it. Narrow (needs an underway re-optimize AND a vroom drop with no vehicle window) and arguably still better than losing the whole ORS order, but the "append as late" design only pays off when a window pass follows it, and here none does.

newHazards.summary: Reset effect can blank Departure Time with no re-seed now that `startTime` left the seed deps
newHazards.detail: The reset effect's deps are `[open, today]`; `today` is recomputed every render from `new Date()`. If the modal is open across midnight and anything re-renders it, `today` changes, the reset effect re-runs and calls `setStartTime("")`, while the seed effect no longer re-runs (its deps `[open, routeSettings?.defaultStartTime]` are unchanged and `seededRef.current` is already true). The field is then silently empty until the operator retypes it — the dispatch would fall back to the server default rather than the shown value. Pre-fix, `startTime` in the seed deps re-seeded it. Vanishingly rare (a dispatch modal held open past midnight) and self-healing on close/reopen; noting it because it is a direct consequence of this round's dep change.

newHazards.summary: Templates modal now discards an operator-chosen departure time on reopen while date/driver still persist
newHazards.detail: templates/[id]/page.tsx has no reset-on-open effect and its DispatchModal stays mounted (rendered with `open={dispatchOpen}` at :1250), so `date` and `driverId` survive a close/reopen. Previously `startTime` survived too (the old effect only ran when `defaultStartTime` changed and `!startTime`). With seededRef cleared on close, reopening re-seeds the tenant default over a time the operator had picked — so the modal now resets one field and keeps two. That is exactly what "seeded once per open, cleared on close" means and it does match routes/page.tsx (which resets everything on open), so it is a design consequence of the ruling rather than an executor error; but on this page it reads as an inconsistency. Cheapest resolution if it bothers the owner: give templates the same reset-on-open block routes/page.tsx has, rather than scoping the ref-clear to unmount.

review.reasoning:
All three round-3 items survive refutation. Finding 1 is fixed at the level the ruling asked for and no softer: I traced an unassigned job from the vroom payload through the parser's sort/dedupe (job id = i+1 confirmed at the request builder, so ascending ids really are original relative order), through applyWindowPass (no feasible slot exists for the pinned fixture, so the not-inserted branch puts it back at min(index 2, len 2) = last), through the two-phase transaction that persists all three stopNumbers, to a result with windowViolations naming it and usedFallback/fallbackReason untouched because nothing throws. I attacked the count check three ways (out-of-range id, id present in both steps and unassigned, empty unassigned with short steps) and it still throws with the original message and counts in every one — the appended ids cannot pad a genuinely short response. REG-B161 is a real value oracle now, with an independently derivable eta (33.36 km / 50 km/h = 40 min → 08:40), and grep proves its `stop-late` fixture appears in no REG-B147 test, so the two cannot pass on each other's order. The documented deviation from the ruling's literal windowEnd "09:00" is correct and the ruling was wrong: a 09:00 close makes the stop feasible and deletes the violation the test exists to pin; the ruled oracle shape is implemented exactly. Finding 0 is fixed identically in both modals, `startTime` is out of the deps, and the clear path holds because neither dep changes on a keystroke; the reopen path works because both modals stay mounted and the close branch clears the ref, and the routes/page reset effect runs before the seed effect in declaration order so the open still lands on the default rather than "".

Nothing needs another fix round: the four new hazards are all minor, three of them are direct consequences of the ruled design rather than executor slips, and none of them changes a persisted value on the paths the batch is about. Two verification items should be closed before the PR merges, and neither is a code change: (1) the ruled mutation probe was NOT run (probe was null in my inputs) — "REG-B147/B161 go red on their own values" is currently argued, not executed, and that probe is the only evidence that the hardened oracles actually bite; (2) the web eslint gate is unverified for an environmental reason — apps/web/node_modules/eslint 8.57.1 against root 9.39.4 makes @typescript-eslint throw before linting anything, which I confirmed read-only from both package.json versions. I closed the substantive half of that gap myself: every problem the root-eslint-9 diagnostic reported exists on master too (`cn` unused at master line 15, `(d: any)` at master line 148), and exhaustive-deps fires elsewhere in the templates file but not on either new seed effect, so this change introduces no new lint surface — the gate needs to run in an installed tree or on CI, not another edit here.
